Identifying of eligible participants;
o Obtaining informed consent from participants;

Reviewing of the medical records to extract relevant information;
o Documentation of patient history, prior treatments, and relevant medical conditions.
Medical information collection from electronic records:
o Accessing electronic health records (RAKUS) to supplement medical histories.
o Extracting of diagnostic reports, imaging results, and treatment plans.
Laboratory data collection:
o Retrieving laboratory test results including blood tests, biopsies, and imaging findings.
o Ensuring accurate documentation and recording of laboratory data.

distribution.title: The project aims to generate fresh insights for scientists in Latvia and more broadly, enriching their academic endeavors in the future. While all investigators are currently engaged in research, project participation will broaden their scientific scope, fostering connections with scholars from other nations through the dissemination of study findings at international conferences and through scientific publications.

dataset.title: Gastric cancer patient data

dmp.description: The project's objective is to generate novel insights and knowledge regarding the risk factors associated with gastric cancer, promote international collaboration, and strengthen the recognition of the University of Latvia. To increase understanding of the significance of risk factors in gastric cancer development, we plan to continue the collection, integration, and analysis of Latvian patient data within the international epidemiological StoP (Stomach Cancer Pooling Project) initiative. Within this project framework, efforts will be directed towards compiling clinical information from the RAKUS (Riga East University hospital) databases, encompassing medical histories, outpatient records, and electronic archives. Subsequently, the gathered data will undergo coding and secure transmission for inclusion in the StoP project's centralized database. It is anticipated that information pertaining to 400 patients will be added to the database. Following data inclusion, endeavours will be made to seek participation in new sub-projects, facilitating epidemiological data analysis and publication authorship. To date, comprehensive data entries encompassing clinical, histological, and epidemiological parameters have been incorporated into the StoP database, comprising a total of 606 gastric cancer patients and 645 individuals constituting the control group. Collaborative efforts with StoP project stakeholders have yielded multiple publications, with findings disseminated through international conference presentations.
